title: 2000 AMC 12 Problem 4
statement: The Fibonacci sequence \(1,\) \(1,\) \(2,\) \(3,\) \(5,\) \(8,\) \(13,\) \(21,\) \(\ldots\) starts with two \(1\)s, and each term afterwards is the sum of its two predecessors. Which one of the ten digits is the last to appear in the units position of a number in the Fibonacci sequence?

solutions.text:
The sequence of units digits begins \[ \begin{gathered} 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 3, 1, 4, 5, 9, \\ 4, 3, 7, 0, 7, 7, 4, 1, 5, 6, \ldots \end{gathered} \]

Scanning this list, the digit \(6\) is the last of the ten digits to appear.

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Track only the units digit of each term
List the units digits until all ten digits have appeared, and note which shows up last
